title: Liverpool’s Alexander Isak expected to be fit ‘around end of March’ – Arne Slot
content:
Arne Slot, the Liverpool head coach, hopes to have Alexander Isak back with his squad by the end of March as the Swedish striker steps up his rehabilitation.

The club’s record signing has been sidelined since suffering a broken leg against Tottenham Hotspur in December.

“Alex has been back on the pitch, not with his football boots but with his running shoes for the first time this week,” Slot said.

“It’s nice for him to go on the pitch and it’s nice for us to see him here but there is still a lot of work to be done when you arrive in the final stages of your rehab. As long as you’re in the gym and not the pitch, that’s not the nicest part.

“The next step is doing work with the ball, which every player likes most. Then the next step is to come into the group and then it takes a while before you’re ready to play. But it’s nice that his rehab goes well – it’s a compliment to him and our medical staff.”

It’s been a difficult season for Isak, who arrived from Newcastle United for a club record £125million fee last summer after a protracted transfer saga. He went on strike to help force the move and needed time to get up to speed at Anfield.

He scored just three goals in 16 appearances for Slot’s side before he was hurt by a challenge from Tottenham defender Micky van de Ven. However, Slot believes that a fully fit Isak could be a huge asset during the run-in as Liverpool look to secure a top-five Premier League finish and chase silverware in the FA Cup and Champions League.

“We expect a different player towards the end of the season to the one we had in the first part,” he added.

“That makes complete sense because I’ve said it a hundred times that we had to give him time. If a player has had four or five months of only individual training, we cannot expect that he is up to speed straight away.

“Unfortunately for him and us, we haven’t used the best Alex yet, but this club and our fans will hopefully see the best Alex this season but, for sure, in the upcoming years.”

Asked if Isak would be back fit around the March international break, Slot joked: “Are you asking this for the Swedish national team coach?

“It will be somewhere around there and then it’s always a question if things go really well or if he gets a bit of a setback. It will be around end of March, start of April, where he is hopefully back with the group.

“When you are back with the group that is not to say you are ready to play, let alone start a game a game of football, because again he’s been out for months. The last time he was out for months we could all see it took him a while before he was the player who we signed from Newcastle.”

Slot confirmed that Jeremie Frimpong remains unavailable for Sunday’s trip to Nottingham Forest but he expects the Dutch right-back to be fit for the home clash with West Ham United the following weekend.
